title: Product search and product details

sourcesRead.contributes: context, verifier notes, six acceptance criteria, out of scope
empty-state mock-up referenced by the fourth criterion (read through transcripts/search-empty-state.png.md)

context: Customers search juices from the top-bar search of an Angular single-page shop. The search view is the hash route /#/search?q=<term>, backed by the REST search endpoint on the same origin. Product detail information includes customer reviews. Verifier notes: dismiss the welcome banner and cookie notice on first visit; prices are rendered with a currency placeholder glyph (e.g. 1.99¤); no login is required for search or reading reviews (story.md#L19-L28).

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Navigating to `/#/search?q=apple` shows the matching products as a grid of cards. Each card shows the product name, its price, and an **Add to Basket** button. The results header reads `Search Results - apple` (the header echoes the exact term that was searched).
acceptanceCriteria.text: Navigating to /#/search?q=apple shows the matching products as a grid of cards. Each card shows the product name, its price, and an Add to Basket button. The results header reads "Search Results - apple" (the header echoes the exact term that was searched).
outcomes: the matching products are shown as a grid of cards
each card shows the product name
each card shows its price
each card shows an "Add to Basket" button
the results header reads "Search Results - apple" (echoes the exact term searched)

acceptanceCriteria.quote: `GET /rest/products/search?q=<term>` returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body of the shape `{"status":"success","data":[ ... ]}`. Every product object in `data` matches `<term>` in its **name or its description**, case-insensitively. For a term that matches nothing, `data` is an empty array (still HTTP 200, still `"status":"success"`).

acceptanceCriteria.quote: For the same term, the set of product names displayed on the `/#/search` results page equals the set of product names returned by `GET /rest/products/search?q=<term>`.

When a search returns no matching products, the results view shows the header `Search Results - <term>`, a **No results found** title, the helper line _Try adjusting your search to find what you're looking for._, and a result count of `0 of 0`.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: The search term is user input and must be handled as literal text. When the term contains characters that are significant in SQL or markup — for example a single apostrophe (`'`), or an SQL-like fragment — the search endpoint must still return a normal HTTP 200 success envelope (with an empty `data` array when nothing matches). It must never return a server-side error status or leak a database engine / query message to the client.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Special characters are treated as data, not code. The search term is user input and must be handled as literal text. When the term contains characters that are significant in SQL or markup (for example a single apostrophe ('), or an SQL-like fragment), the search endpoint must still return a normal HTTP 200 success envelope (with an empty data array when nothing matches). It must never return a server-side error status or leak a database engine / query message to the client.
outcomes: a term containing a single apostrophe (') returns a normal HTTP 200 success envelope
a term containing an SQL-like fragment returns a normal HTTP 200 success envelope
the term is handled as literal text: data is an empty array when nothing matches
never a server-side error status
no database engine / query message leaked to the client

acceptanceCriteria.quote: `GET /rest/products/{id}/reviews` returns HTTP 200 with a body of the shape `{"status":"success","data":[ ... ]}`. Each review object carries at least a `message` string and an `author`. For product `1` the listing is non-empty.
acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /rest/products/{id}/reviews returns HTTP 200 with a body of the shape {"status":"success","data":[ ... ]}. Each review object carries at least a message string and an author. For product 1 the listing is non-empty.

body of the shape {"status":"success","data":[ ... ]}

endpoints.request: query parameter q = the search term (story.md#L34)
path parameter id = product id (product 1 per story.md#L42)

auth.mechanism: none: no login is required for search or for reading reviews

rules.text: A search result matches the term in its name or its description, case-insensitively.
Search and review listing responses use the envelope {"status":"success","data":[ ... ]}.
The search term is user input and must be handled as literal text; characters significant in SQL or markup never cause a server-side error status or a leaked database engine / query message.
The results header echoes the exact term that was searched: "Search Results - <term>".

testData.strategy: none created: read-only catalogue and existing reviews. Terms: "apple" (story.md#L32); a term that matches nothing (G1); terms containing a single apostrophe (') and an SQL-like fragment (story.md#L40). Reviews are read for product 1 (story.md#L42).
testData.constraints: Writing reviews is out of scope (story.md#L46), so product 1's reviews must not be seeded by the evaluation. Dismiss the welcome banner and cookie notice on first visit (story.md#L26).
